description: Start a conversation, or reply on an item you made (item_id). To start one, contact needs your person's name and an email address or a phone number: ask them first, and send only what they agree to give this business; never make them up. A reply needs no contact.

access_token.description: Capability secret returned when the item was created without an account.

contact.description: To start a conversation: your person's details, as they agreed to give them to this business, as for any new request (their name, and an email address or a phone number). Ask them first; never make them up, and never send your own. Leave it out on a reply.

email.description: An email address the business can answer them at: one that receives mail, not a no-reply one.

locale.description: The language they want answers in: en, pt.

name.description: Their name, as they want the business to use it: with a letter in it and no @. Never a placeholder (N/A, Test, {{name}}).

phone.description: A phone number the business can reach them on, with its country code: +351 912 345 678. 6 to 20 digits, no letters (no extension), and only spaces, +, -, (, ), . or / between them.

idempotency_key.description: Same key + same request = same answer. Required for agents. Make it a fresh random UUID per request, never one made from the request itself: a retry of a create with a random key gets its access token again, so a key anyone could work out would give it to them.

item_id.description: Reply on an existing item; omit to start a new conversation.

key.description: The person's key (sdkey1_…), if that is all you have: it is exchanged once for a pass, which comes back in identity.passes — keep the pass and send it next time instead. Never stored.

pass.description: The person's passes (sdpass1_…), space-separated, at most 8: presented to the network that issued each, so the business recognises the customer. Or send them in the Sdi-Pass header. Never stored.

name: send_message
title: Send a message
